title: La mer
hook: The sea in three sketches, painted with an orchestra instead of a brush.

painting.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Debussy kept a print of this wave in his study and asked for it on the cover of the first edition of La mer in 1905.
painting.medium: Woodblock print; ink and color on paper

facts: Debussy wrote *La mer* between 1903 and 1905. He began it far from the coast, in Burgundy, and said he preferred the seas of paintings and books to the real one. He corrected the proofs in the summer of 1905 at a hotel in Eastbourne, on the English Channel.

He called it “three symphonic sketches” and avoided the word symphony. There are few tunes in the usual sense: a short [[motif|motif]] grows, changes colour and turns into a new one, the way one wave turns into the next.

The first performance, in Paris on 15 October 1905, was a disappointment. One critic wrote that he could not hear, see or smell the sea. It became a success in 1908, when Debussy conducted it himself.
Debussy owned a print of Hokusai’s *Great Wave* and asked for it to be used on the cover of the first edition.
bigPicture.inOneLine: the sea waking from dawn to noon (I), waves at play (II), a storm between wind and water (III).

movements.heading: De l'aube à midi sur la mer
movements.title: De l'aube à midi sur la mer (From Dawn to Noon on the Sea)
movements.summary: The sea before sunrise, still and dark, slowly fills with light and movement. The music never repeats itself for long; it swells, breaks and re-forms. It ends at noon, in a blaze of brass.

mainIdeas.name: The call
mainIdeas.description: a short, rising figure for cor anglais and [[muted|muted]] trumpet together, heard near the start. It will come back in the last movement.
The noon [[chorale|chorale]]: a broad, slow melody for the brass at the very end.

stops.hear: A low, soft rumble from the timpani and double basses; harps pluck; muted violins shimmer above
stops.happening: Darkness before dawn. One low note is held underneath, a [[pedal-note|pedal note]]

stops.hear: A short call from the cor anglais and muted trumpet playing together
The pace picks up: woodwinds rock back and forth, horns answer, harps ripple
stops.happening: The sea wakes. The main part of the movement begins

stops.hear: A warm, swaying melody low in the strings, rich and dark
stops.happening: The cellos, split into four groups, play in [[divisi|divisi]]. A famous page of the score

stops.hear: Waves of sound build up, each one a little higher

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: The brass play a slow, solemn melody; cymbals and a gong crown it with a final crash
stops.happening: The noon chorale. The sun is at its height

notice: Listen to the very end. The brass chorale returns at the end of the third movement, louder and faster.

movements.heading: Jeux de vagues
movements.title: Jeux de vagues (Play of the Waves)
movements.summary: The lightest movement, close to a [[scherzo|scherzo]]. Spray, glitter and sudden gusts. Nothing stays in one place for more than a few seconds.

stops.hear: Trembling strings, a harp [[glissando|glissando]], a tap on the triangle, a flicker from the cor anglais
Little phrases tossed between oboe, flute and cor anglais; the glockenspiel sparkles
Trills in the woodwinds and violins; the music becomes busier
The whole orchestra swells into larger waves, then breaks apart

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The sound thins out: a harp, the glockenspiel, a few soft notes from the flute
stops.happening: The waves die away. The movement ends almost in silence

notice: Count how many instruments get a solo moment. Debussy gives almost every one a few seconds in the light.

movements.heading: Dialogue du vent et de la mer
movements.title: Dialogue du vent et de la mer (Dialogue of the Wind and the Sea)
movements.summary: A storm. The low strings and drums growl, the wind howls in the woodwinds, and the call from the first movement returns. After a calm middle, the noon chorale comes back in triumph.

stops.hear: A dark rumble from cellos, basses, timpani and bass drum; sudden gusts in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The wind rises over the sea

stops.hear: The muted trumpet plays the short call from the first movement
The storm drops. An oboe and a flute sing a long, tender melody over high violins
stops.happening: A calm in the middle of the storm

stops.hear: The rumbling returns and gathers speed; strings and brass trade blows
stops.happening: Wind and sea answer each other

stops.hear: The brass ring out the slow noon chorale from the first movement, now loud and fast

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A headlong rush; timpani and brass hammer out the final chords

threads.title: The call and the chorale
threads.body: Two ideas from the first movement return in the last, so the three sketches become one picture.

threads.title: Colour as shape
threads.body: Debussy builds each movement from changes of sound: which instrument plays, how high, how loud. That is where to listen.

threads.title: A Japanese wave
threads.body: Like Hokusai’s print, the music is precise in its details and huge in its effect.
